changes.before: Move Notes to a separate module Atlas::Notes body, leaving TITLE unqualified inside title. What happens?
changes.after: A constant is a name for a value that code normally keeps the same. Ruby uses the surrounding written scopes when looking up this name.

before: Atlas::Notes means the Notes constant inside Atlas. Constants begin with uppercase letters. A constant can refer to a mutable object; the name alone does not freeze that object.

A nested module Notes body inside module Atlas has Atlas in its lexical nesting, so unqualified TITLE can resolve there. Opening module Atlas::Notes directly does not create the same lexical nesting. Use Atlas::TITLE explicitly when that is the intended dependency.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
module Atlas
  TITLE = "outer"
  module Notes
    def self.title
      TITLE
    end
  end
end
puts Atlas::Notes.title
```
Expected output or behavior: outer. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
